A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSR2-GCD work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SSR2-GCD results on eight datasets, component ablations, representation analyses, sensitivity tests, and computational costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds category-count sensitivity results and counts of removed prompt tags.

M1.justification: The reported warm-up objective changes: v1 uses the full SSR2 loss, whereas v2 Equations (9)–(10) exclude the pseudo-label compression term until the alignment stage. Equation (8) also corrects the text-branch compression input from image to text embeddings. RTA, the architecture, co-teaching, and inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight generic and fine-grained datasets and GCD tasks. The class-imbalanced Flowers102 analysis moved into v2's main text already appears in v1 Appendix B.3. The new classifier-dimension sweep changes model settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched benchmark, component, loss-function, prompt-quality, and uni-modal comparisons. CICO and the GCD/SimGCD adaptations already appear in v1's appendix. Newly cited related work does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix B.8 introduces a Flowers102 classifier-output-dimension sweep around K=102, reporting NMI and ARI alongside ACC. The reported warm-up objective also changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Existing dataset splits, backbones, augmentations, batch size, and 200-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds robustness testing against misspecified category counts and quantifies overlap between unknown-category names and prompt tags. Conversely, its candidate-count analysis retains only CIFAR-10 and Stanford Cars, removing v1 Figure 6's CIFAR-100 and Flowers102 panels. The remaining ablations and robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three trials with seeds 0, 1, and 2, mean accuracy with standard deviations in Tables A.5–A.6, and uncertainty shading for the alignment-weight sweep. No changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 and matched appendix performance and cost tables retain their numerical values. New Table B.7 reports 90, 83, 43, and 17 removed tags for CUB, Cars, Flowers102, and Pets. New Figure B.7 reports category-count sensitivity, including sharp deterioration with too few clusters. Two candidate-count result grids are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification receives limited changes: Equation (8) corrects the text-branch embedding argument, and v2 Equation (9) explicitly defines the supervised-only warm-up objective. The coding-rate definitions, consistency ratio renamed from Re to rho, and existing rank rationale otherwise remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central SSR2, RTA, and benchmark-performance claims remain. However, v2 Section 4.2 explicitly restricts the first-work claim about addressing imbalanced compression to GCD and omits v1 Section 3.2's additional first-work claim about rethinking inter-modal alignment. Its stronger abstract emphasis on intra-modal consistency reiterates an existing finding.

C2.justification: v2 adds an applicability qualification concerning sensitivity to underestimated category counts and relative robustness to overestimation, plus a rationale for avoiding unreliable pseudo-label guidance during warm-up. It removes v1's explicit limitations discussion about equal treatment of modalities and candidate-dependent overhead, although measured computational costs remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the abstract and documents removed-tag counts for the existing prompt-filtering experiment. The PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents or availability. Hardware, optimizer, learning rates, augmentation instructions, and most implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 2 substantially expands research positioning through method-specific discussions of uni-modal and multi-modal GCD, including a critique of GET's known-category textual inversion supervision. It adds references on k-means++, classical k-means, and textual inversion, while removing the SCAN citation. This extends the earlier introduction and pipeline discussion considerably.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites prose across the main paper and appendix, inserts a related-work section, reorganizes the training description, and moves the imbalance analysis into the main text. Section headings, terminology, and mathematical labels are revised throughout; the limitations paragraph is replaced by acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively rearranged and resized, including moving and redrawing the appendix imbalance visualization as main Figure 6 and enlarging appendix embedding visualizations. v2 adds a tag-count table and category-count plot, reduces four candidate-count panels to two, and relabels axes and captions. Figure 4(b,c) receives dataset labels inconsistent with the unchanged v1 plots.

improvement.justification: Corrected loss specification, explicit warm-up treatment, expanded research context, code-access information, and category-count robustness evidence improve clarity and assessability. Benchmark performance evidence is unchanged. Removing two sensitivity panels and explicit limitations, alongside confusing Figure 4 dataset labels, offsets some benefits and limits the net improvement.
